findings.description: Across the five low-resource targets (BN, AZ, MN, MR, KA), both Method M-static and Method M-dynamic achieved higher COMET scores than supervised fine-tuning for every language.

Low-resource BLEU improvements were not fully consistent: both Method M variants improved BN, AZ, and MN, but M-static decreased MR and tied KA, while M-dynamic decreased KA and improved MR only slightly.

On the high-resource DE and ZH pairs, Method M-dynamic exceeded supervised fine-tuning on both COMET and BLEU, whereas Method M-static was mixed, decreasing both metrics on DE and differing only marginally from supervised on ZH.

In the four-language average, Method M-dynamic with FILTER and NN outperformed every REINFORCE and PPO variant on BLEU, COMET-KIWI, COMET, and XCOMET; it was the best system on the first three metrics, while Method M-static had the highest XCOMET score.
Every reported REINFORCE and PPO configuration scored below ordinary supervised fine-tuning on all four metrics in the four-language average.
For Method M-dynamic, adding FILTER and NN increased all four averaged metrics relative to the otherwise reported dynamic configuration without those data techniques.
The main-table results are three-seed means without standard deviations or significance tests, so the package does not establish whether the reported differences are statistically reliable.
COMET-KIWI was used as Method M's training signal, the RL reward, the early-stopping criterion, and a reported evaluation metric, while COMET, XCOMET, and BLEU provided additional evaluation views.
